answer: Radio coverage witnessing: each identity runs a physical hotspot that broadcasts a signed beacon at random times, and the network picks nearby hotspots at random to report hearing it at a signal strength that fits its registered spot, say a farm orchard. Hotspots heard from the same small map cell split one reward, so ten identities stacked in one shed earn as one; each extra identity needs its own radio, power and separate site. Limit: a ring of colluding hotspots can forge reports, so random witness choice and audits matter. No ivory-tower theory or sonnet replaces real hardware here.
